Now I have comprehensive information. Here's a detailed exploration report on `@pantoken/components` and the broader architecture:

---

## **1. Authoring Records: TypeScript Types & Field Structure**

**Type Definitions:**
[lib/define.ts](formats/components/src/lib/define.ts#L1-L94)

```typescript
interface Definition {
  name: string;
  kind: "component" | "utility" | "rule" | "declaration";
  rules(prefix: string, options?: ComponentOptions): string;
  css(options?: ComponentOptions): string;
}

interface DefineInput {
  name: string;
  css: (p: string, options?: ComponentOptions) => string;
}

interface ComponentOptions {
  prefix?: string | null;      // "instui" → .instui-button, falsy → .button
  theme?: "rebrand" | "canvas" | "canvasHighContrast";
}
```

**Factories:**
- [`defineComponent(input)`](formats/components/src/lib/define.ts#L88) — component record
- [`defineUtility(input)`](formats/components/src/lib/define.ts#L90) — utility class set
- [`defineRule(input)`](formats/components/src/lib/define.ts#L92) — reset/base rule
- [`defineDeclaration(input)`](formats/components/src/lib/define.ts#L94) — @property registration

**Record Fields:**
- `name` — exported identifier + cssdoc `@component`/`@utility` name
- `css: (p, options?) => string` — template-literal builder receiving prefix `p` and theme. Returns doc comment + CSS body. Prefix is passed as `ns(p)` (e.g., `"instui-"`).
- Metadata (modifiers, parts, etc.) — plain-string JSDoc comments; **no backticks allowed** inside (see user memory: `js-ts-gotchas.md`)
- Modifiers — discovered from cssdoc `@modifier` lines; aliases/deprecated variants auto-generated by [aliases.ts](formats/components/src/lib/aliases.ts)
- **NO explicit modifier list in the type** — modifiers live in the cssdoc comment and are parsed at cssdoc-generation time

**Sentinel Pattern:**
[sentinel.ts](formats/components/src/lib/sentinel.ts) — `.css` source files use `SENTINEL = "pfx-"` (lowercase, dash-suffixed) instead of interpolated `${p}`. Build-time `replaceAll("pfx-", ns(prefix))` swaps it. This keeps `.css` files lintable by cssdoc and stylelint (uppercase `PFX-` would break cssdoc inference).

---

## **2. CSS Emission Pipeline: Records → dist/components.css, base.css, fonts.css**

**Build task sequence** (from [vite.config.ts](formats/components/vite.config.ts#L20-L36)):

```
build:
  1. vp run @pantoken/plugin-theme-custom-media#build
  2. node scripts/component-styles.ts        ← .css files → component-styles.ts
  3. node scripts/generate.ts                ← Aggregate sheets (base, components, utilities, etc.)
  4. node scripts/build-entries.ts           ← Per-component .css + utility .css exports
  5. vp pack                                 ← Rolldown bundle
  6. node scripts/post-pack.ts               ← Post-pack fixups
  7. node scripts/generate-model.ts          ← dist/model.json (cssdoc entries)
```

**Script Details:**

| Script | Input | Output | Purpose |
|--------|-------|--------|---------|
| [component-styles.ts](formats/components/scripts/component-styles.ts#L1-80) | `src/components/**/*.css`, `src/utilities/**/*.css` | `src/generated/component-styles.ts` | Compile `.css` source files (with `pfx-` sentinel) into TS string consts. Uses postcss to expand utility selectors. Retains cssdoc comments. |
| [generate.ts](formats/components/scripts/generate.ts#L1-50) | `src/index.ts` (exports all records) | `generated/base.css`, `generated/components.css`, `generated/utilities.css`, etc. | Instantiate each record's `.css()` builder with prefix `"instui"` and theme, concatenate into aggregate sheets. |
| [build-entries.ts](formats/components/scripts/build-entries.ts#L1-50) | `src/components/`, `src/utilities/` | `generated/<name>.css` per component + per-utility | Write individual component `.css` and utility `.css` files for subpath exports (e.g., `@pantoken/components/button.css`). |
| [generate-model.ts](formats/components/scripts/generate-model.ts#L1-30) | `dist/components.css`, `dist/utilities.css` (minified) | `dist/model.json` | Parse aggregated minified CSS via [@pantoken/cssdoc-model](tools/cssdoc-model) to produce cssdoc `CssDocEntry[]` for editor hints + documentation. |

**Key Insight:** The `.css` source is the authoring truth; records pull from generated consts at build time and remain prefix-agnostic at runtime (consumers pass `prefix` at call time).

---

## **3. Structured CSS & AST Availability**

**No standalone programmatic AST is exported.** However:

- **Test-time parsing:** [button.test.ts](formats/components/tests/components/button.test.ts) and [icon.test.ts](formats/components/tests/utilities/icon.test.ts) import `postcss` to parse emitted CSS for assertion (e.g., checking for specific selectors/rules).
- **cssdoc model (published):** [generate-model.ts](formats/components/scripts/generate-model.ts) uses [@pantoken/cssdoc-model](tools/cssdoc-model) to emit `dist/model.json` — a published `CssDocEntry[]` with parsed structure (selectors, modifiers, parts) suitable for LSP/editor lookups and runtime (e.g., TinyMCE's component/icon pickers).
- **Validation at build:** [_validate.ts](formats/components/tests/_validate.ts) uses `@cssdoc/core`'s `parseCssDocs()` to ensure every record parses to exactly one cssdoc entry + no token drift per theme.

**Modifier resolution:** No programmatic `.component(...).getModifiers()` — modifiers are discovered by parsing the cssdoc `@modifier` lines. The `withAliases` / `withSizeAliases` post-processors **mutate CSS text** (regex-based brace scanning) to clone rules.

---

## **4. How Modifiers Work & Programmatic Resolution**

**Modifier Convention (RSCSS):**
- **Key-value compound:** `.instui-button.-color-primary`, `.instui-button.-size-lg`
- **Booleans (presence = true):** `.instui-button.-clickable`, `.instui-button.-condensed`
- **Default-on boolean (inverted):** `.instui-button.-without-background`
- **Size aliases (first-class):** Both short (`.-size-sm`) and long (`.-size-small`) are emitted by [withSizeAliases()](formats/components/src/lib/aliases.ts#L80-100)
- **Deprecated/aliased modifiers:** Discovered from cssdoc `@alias {@link -canonical}` or `@deprecated {@link -canonical}` via regex [DEPRECATED_ALIAS](formats/components/src/lib/aliases.ts#L18) pattern; [withAliases()](formats/components/src/lib/aliases.ts#L108-130) clones canonical rules under alias selectors.

**Scope-relative globals:** [globalModifierSelector()](packages/utils/src/index.ts) emits `:where(*).--name` (triple-class specificity) for global utilities (`--bg-secondary`, `--margin-bottom-small`), which deterministically outrank component-modifiers (0,2,0) regardless of import order.

**Programmatic Resolution:**
- **At build time:** post-processors run on raw CSS text (no AST); prefix swap happens before aliases.
- **At runtime:** No built-in resolver — consumers match selectors manually. `model.json` exports provide cssdoc parsed structure for tooling to query modifiers by component.
- **Example (conceptual):** `.instui-button.-color-secondary` is resolved by matching against `button` record's rules; the CSS declaration block is determined at build time (no dynamic substitution).

## **6. Dependency Rules: @pantoken/tokens IR & @pantoken/model Types**

**Canonical flow:**
```
@pantoken/core (GitHub-only upstream) 
  ↓ builds once
@pantoken/tokens (IR vendor: Token[], deprecation ledger)
  ↓
@pantoken/model (zero-dep types: Token, Theme, TokenMeta, DeprecationEntry)
  ↓
formats/* (depend on model + tokens, NEVER core)
  ↓
renderers/* (depend on format packages, never core)
```

**Why?** 
- `core` depends on `@instructure/instructure-design-tokens` (GitHub-only, not on npm).
- Every consumer needs the IR types → zero-dep `model` lives separately.
- Formats import type-only from `model` + value from `tokens` to avoid pulling `core`'s upstream.
- Example: [components/package.json](formats/components/package.json#L29-L31) → `@pantoken/tokens`, `@pantoken/utils`, `@pantoken/scaffold-base` (no `core`).
- Example: [scss/package.json](formats/scss/package.json#L33-L35) → same pattern.

**Runtime-safe:** `@pantoken/components` and `@pantoken/web-components` export into browsers → **Node-free** (no `node:*` imports). Postcss usage confined to build scripts, never bundled.

First, your two questions:

**Can we use juice?** Yes — and it's a better fit than I assumed. juice 12.2.0 has `inlineContent(html, css, opts)`, `resolveCSSVariables`, `preservePseudos`/`ignoredPseudos`, and a `juice/client` browser entry. The catch is it's an HTML-in/HTML-out tool, so to get a *declaration map* we run it at build time against one synthetic probe element per selector and read the resulting `style` attribute back. That keeps the work linear per selector instead of exponential per modifier combination, and juice handles specificity and shorthand for us. juice stays out of the runtime bundle. One hard security rule: only `inlineContent`/`inlineDocument`, never `juiceFile`/`juiceResources` — those fetch remote resources and would be an SSRF surface.

**Consumers option 3** was per-component markup helpers — `renderButton({ color: "primary", children: "Save" })` → `<button style="...">Save</button>`. That means owning the HTML structure of all 34 components, not just their styles. I've excluded it.

## Plan: `@pantoken/inline-styles` base package

A new `formats/inline-styles` package flattens pantoken component CSS into `style` attributes at build time using juice, ships the result as static JSON, and exposes a zero-dependency, Node-free runtime that merges base + modifier declarations. `@pantoken/email` then consumes and re-exports it without breaking its existing token-value API.

**Steps**

**Phase 1 — Scaffold** (blocks everything)
1. Create `formats/inline-styles/` modeled on `formats/scss` + `platforms/email`. Deps: `@pantoken/model`, `@pantoken/tokens`, `@pantoken/utils`, `juice`; devDep `@pantoken/components`. No `@pantoken/core`.
2. Add `juice` to the `pnpm-workspace.yaml` catalog — verify with `npm view juice version`, don't pin from memory.
3. Wire the build task order `node scripts/generate.ts` → `vp pack`, mirroring the components build.

**Phase 2 — Build tier** (*depends on Phase 1*)
4. Pre-resolve `var(--instui-*)` and `light-dark()` to concrete values via `resolveTokens(tokens, { mode })` before juice ever sees the CSS — juice can't resolve `light-dark()`.
5. Probe each selector (base `.instui-button`, then each modifier compound) through juice; selector inventory comes from `@pantoken/components/dist/model.json`, so aliases and deprecated modifiers are covered for free.
6. Bucket what can't be inlined — `:hover`/`:focus`, `::before` icon painters, `@media`, `@scope`, child combinators — into a parallel `fallbackCss` string per component.

**Phase 3 — Runtime tier** (*depends on Phase 2, parallel with Phase 4*)
7. `inlineStyle()`, `inlineStyleObject()`, `fallbackCss()` — zero deps, browser-safe.
8. Per-theme-mode subpath exports so a consumer ships one map, not all six.

**Phase 4 — Document tier** (*depends on Phase 2, parallel with Phase 3*)
9. `@pantoken/inline-styles/html` — `inlineHtml(html, opts)` wrapping `juice.inlineContent`, with `browser` field → `juice/client`.

**Phase 5 — Integrate** (*depends on 3 & 4*)
10. `@pantoken/email` re-exports the new API; existing `light`/`dark`/`emailTokens` untouched.
11. Tests, including a guard that the runtime entry has no `node:` import and no juice import.
12. Docs: README, `docs/compatibility.md`, `docs/architecture/overview.md`.
13. `ASSURANCE.md` + `SECURITY.md` — new input surface (arbitrary HTML into cheerio), control "no remote fetching", and the note that `inlineHtml` doesn't sanitize.
14. Changeset.

**Relevant files**
- `formats/inline-styles/` — new package
- `platforms/email/src/index.ts` — reuse the `resolveTokens` + `camelCase` + icon-skip (`token.meta?.kind === "icon"`) pattern; add re-exports
- `formats/components/dist/model.json` — authoritative component + modifier inventory
- `formats/components/vite.config.ts` and `scripts/build-entries.ts` — templates for the build task DAG and subpath export generation
- `pnpm-workspace.yaml` — juice catalog entry
- `ASSURANCE.md`, `SECURITY.md`

1. `vp run build` in the new package; `vp test` there and in `platforms/email`.
2. Assert no `var(` or `light-dark(` substring survives in any generated JSON value.
3. Bundle guard: packed `src/index.ts` contains no `node:` and no `cheerio`.
4. `vp check --fix`, then `pnpm run ready` + `pnpm run check:publish`.
5. `vp test --coverage` last.

- Base package, not email-only — Pendo, TinyMCE, CMS fields, and embedded 3rd-party HTML have the same constraint.

- `@tsdown/css` — inlines and minifies CSS imported with `?inline` into TypeScript

**One file per theme OR one file with theme-aware tokens?**

**Answer: One `components.css` file using theme-scoped token variables + `@media (--custom-media)` queries.**

Evidence:
- [billboard.css line 91](formats/components/src/components/billboard/billboard.css#L91): `@media (--theme-canvas), (--theme-canvas-high-contrast)`

**How it works**:
1. [scripts/component-styles.ts](formats/components/scripts/component-styles.ts) runs PostCSS with `@pantoken/plugin-theme-custom-media` plugin
2. For each component `.css` file, the plugin **processes three theme passes** (rebrand, canvas, canvasHighContrast)
3. Each pass evaluates `@media (--theme-canvas)` → includes/excludes blocks per theme
4. Generated constants: `export const buttonByTheme = { rebrand: "...", canvas: "..." }`
5. [define.ts](formats/components/src/lib/define.ts#L67) builds the record once per theme and caches the modifiers

**Not global theme switching**: Each emitted component CSS is **theme-bound at generation time**, not runtime-switchable. You choose a theme when building the CSS, not in the browser.

---

| Metric | Finding |
|--------|---------|
| **Statically inlinable CSS** | ~15–30% (base properties only) |
| **Requires pseudo-class/element CSS** | ~70–85% |
| **Multi-part components (≥2 sub-parts)** | 37 of 71 components (52%) |
| **Theme-aware CSS** | 100% (uses custom-media queries) |
| **Pseudo-elements (`::before`, `::after`)** | ~70% of components |
| **Child combinator selectors** | ~90% of components |
| **`:has()` selectors** | ~30% of components |
| **`@media`, `@supports` at-rules** | ~55% of components |

**Feasibility of build-time inlining**: 
- ✅ Possible for **root-level text/color/sizing properties** on simple components (badge, pill, metric)
- ❌ **Not practical** for interactive state (button, checkbox, form fields) or complex layouts (table, drawer-layout, modal)
- 🟡 **Hybrid approach**: Inline root styles + load a companion CSS file for pseudo-classes, pseudo-elements, and state transitions

Emit `style="..."` inline declarations for pantoken components, for renderers that can't use a
`<style>` block or external stylesheet (email, embedded 3rd-party HTML, Pendo, CMS fields).

- Scope: component flattening — `inlineStyle("button", { color: "primary", size: "lg" })`.
- Placement: new base package `formats/inline-styles`; `@pantoken/email` consumes/re-exports it.
- Outputs day one: style-attribute string + camelCased style object (React `CSSProperties` / RN).

- Use **juice** (v12.2.0, ESM-only), build-time only.
- **Coverage: as broad as possible** — all 71 component entries + 14 utilities.
- **All 6 theme x mode maps**, and it must work with `@pantoken/plugin-custom-theme-colors`.
- Excluded: per-component HTML markup helpers, CLI.

`@pantoken/plugin-custom-theme-colors` lets a user supply an arbitrary brand hex at runtime
(`deriveCustomColorScale(hex)`, dependency-free OKLCH, browser-safe) or flip
`data-pantoken-color="navy|blue|...|custom"` on an element. Arbitrary hex cannot be baked at
build time. Therefore the generated maps must **preserve `var(--instui-*)` references**, and
resolution must happen at **runtime** against a substitutable token map.

`@pantoken/utils`) does the substitution in the runtime tier, where the caller can override.

```
inlineStyle("button", { color: "primary" })                       // baked theme map
inlineStyle("button", { color: "primary" }, {
  tokens: deriveCustomColorScale("#e62429")                        // custom brand overrides
})
```

- `@pantoken/email` = `platforms/email`. Exports only `light`/`dark`/`emailTokens(mode)` — camelCased

  `::before`/`::after` glyph masks, `@scope`, `@media (--theme-*)`, `@supports`, `:has()`,

  probes need a parent chain (`<table class="instui-table"><tr class="row">`).

## Goal
Emit `style="..."` inline declarations for pantoken components, for renderers that can't use a
`<style>` block or external stylesheet (email, embedded 3rd-party HTML, Pendo, CMS fields).

## Decisions (confirmed with user)
- Scope: component flattening — `inlineStyle("button", { color: "primary", size: "lg" })`.
- Placement: new base package `formats/inline-styles`; `@pantoken/email` consumes/re-exports it.
- Outputs day one: style-attribute string + camelCased style object (React `CSSProperties` / RN).
- Non-inlinable rules dropped from the inline map, **exposed separately** as `fallbackCss`.
- Use **juice** (v12.2.0, ESM-only), build-time only.
- **Coverage: as broad as possible** — all 71 component entries + 14 utilities.
- **All 6 theme x mode maps**, and it must work with `@pantoken/plugin-custom-theme-colors`.
- Excluded: per-component HTML markup helpers, CLI.

## THE PIVOTAL CONSTRAINT: custom theme colors
`@pantoken/plugin-custom-theme-colors` lets a user supply an arbitrary brand hex at runtime
(`deriveCustomColorScale(hex)`, dependency-free OKLCH, browser-safe) or flip
`data-pantoken-color="navy|blue|...|custom"` on an element. Arbitrary hex cannot be baked at
build time. Therefore the generated maps must **preserve `var(--instui-*)` references**, and
resolution must happen at **runtime** against a substitutable token map.

Consequence: run juice with `resolveCSSVariables: false`. Pantoken's own resolver (from
`@pantoken/utils`) does the substitution in the runtime tier, where the caller can override.

```
inlineStyle("button", { color: "primary" })                       // baked theme map
inlineStyle("button", { color: "primary" }, {
  tokens: deriveCustomColorScale("#e62429")                        // custom brand overrides
})
```

## Key research findings
- `@pantoken/email` = `platforms/email`. Exports only `light`/`dark`/`emailTokens(mode)` — camelCased
  maps of resolved token values. Deps: `@pantoken/tokens`, `@pantoken/model`, `@pantoken/utils`.
- `@pantoken/components`: **71 entries** in `COMPONENTS` (34 root + 37 sub-parts like `table.row`,
  `modal.header`, `tabs.panel`), 14 utilities, 2 rules, 2 declarations. Per-component `dist/*.css`
  plus subpath exports incl. `"./*.css"` wildcard.
- **Only ~15-30% of a typical component's CSS is inlinable.** The rest is `:hover`/`:focus`/`:checked`,
  `::before`/`::after` glyph masks, `@scope`, `@media (--theme-*)`, `@supports`, `:has()`,
  child combinators, `transition`, `@property`, `::backdrop`. This is a real limit, not a bug —
  `fallbackCss` is the primary mitigation and must be first-class, not an afterthought.
- Components CSS uses `@scope (.pfx-button) { & { … } }`. cheerio/juice do NOT understand `@scope` —
  it must be flattened to plain selectors before juice sees it.

  probes need a parent chain (`<table class="instui-table"><tr class="row">`).
- Themes are resolved at generation time: `component-styles.ts` emits
  `buttonByTheme = { rebrand, canvas, canvasHighContrast }` via
  `@pantoken/plugin-theme-custom-media`. So `@media (--theme-*)` is already gone per theme.
- `dist/model.json` = `CssDocEntry[]` with `modifiers[]` (incl. `deprecated.canonical`, `pattern`),

  This is the authoritative selector + modifier inventory.

  scripts. No lightningcss in the repo.

  flattens CSS nesting, Selectors L4 specificity, `juice/client` browser entry.

     `resolveTokens(tokens, { mode })`, icons skipped per the email package rule.

   - Report anything still non-portable so callers can see it rather than shipping broken email.

     with the normalized pantoken stylesheet. juice is a real dependency here only;
